content.comment_body: Hello, I'm running a test program to explore menu navigation on the [product_name] operator device. In the [product_name] simulation, I can switch pages and adjust the counter using cursor keys (C1, C2, C3, C4) without issues. However, during actual testing on both the [product_name] basis module and the operator device, I have to hold ESC while pressing the cursor keys for navigation; pressing only the cursor keys doesn't work.
This behavior is standard because of how the [product_name] and the operator device are designed. There's nothing unexpected about this.

1) Is there any method to avoid having to press ESC? 2) I want the navigation to match the experience in simulation—cursor keys alone should work. Also, I don't want the device to switch from the "Message text" to other settings pages. Ideally, in start mode, the operator device would show only the contents of the "Message text" block, similar to what appears on the web server.

1) Unfortunately, the ESC key is mandatory—you can't bypass it. 2) Can you clarify exactly what you'd like to see when the [product_name] device enters RUN mode? From what you're describing, it sounds like you should activate message texts (through configuration) by means of a button press, rather than having them always on. Without a screenshot or your program file, it's difficult to be precise; it would help if you could share either, especially showing how you connected the message texts in your program. Otherwise, both you and respondents will need to make lots of guesses.

No, pressing ESC together with the relevant cursor key is what signals to the [product_name] to act within the program. I wish things were simpler! Simulation is just a supportive tool and not identical to processing on the actual device. In fact, even in the simulation, only one message text is activated at a time. The key difference is: the screen of the [product_name] or operator device can only show one message text, but the simulation may display all. Still, only one is active. If you'd like to use the same cursor key for different setpoints, you need to implement a lock mechanism, for example, by using message texts.
Given your setup with only four setpoints, you could configure it so that a single message text block is sufficient.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are frustrated by differences between navigation in [product_name] simulation software and on the actual hardware, particularly the requirement to combine ESC and cursor keys for navigation in real use. This inconsistency makes it harder to replicate simulated workflows on the real device and causes confusion for those expecting simulation and device behavior to match closely.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want to navigate using just the cursor keys on the operator device, similar to the simulation, without involving the ESC key. Additionally, they wish for the device to display only the message text on startup, replicating the output shown by the web server.
